name: Gratitude Practice
intro: Welcome. Right now, we're going to practice something simple but powerful.
Gratitude isn't about pretending everything is fine.
It's about finding what's real and good, even in the middle of what's hard.
Take a deep breath. Let your body settle.
Open your heart just a little. That's all it takes.
body: Think of your body. Not its flaws. Its function.
Your lungs are breathing without you asking them to.
Your heart is beating. Your eyes can see. Your ears can hear this voice.
These are not small things. They are miraculous things that we forget to notice.
Take a moment to silently say thank you to your body for carrying you this far.
Now think of one person who has shown you kindness.
It doesn't have to be someone close. Maybe a stranger who smiled. A friend who listened.
Hold their face in your mind. Feel what their kindness meant to you.
We are held by more love than we usually let ourselves feel.
Silently thank that person. Let the warmth of it fill your chest.
Think of something simple that brought you comfort recently.
A warm drink. Sunlight through a window. A song that hit just right.
Happiness doesn't always come in big moments. It hides in small ones.
The ones we rush past. The ones we forget by evening.
Right now, remember one. Savor it. Let it matter.
Consider a difficulty you've faced. Something that was genuinely hard.
Can you find one thing it taught you? One way it shaped you?
This isn't about toxic positivity. It's about recognizing your own growth.
The hard things didn't break you. They built something in you.
You can be grateful for the lesson without being grateful for the pain.
Finally, turn the gratitude inward.
Thank yourself for showing up today. For choosing to pause and feel.
In a world that moves so fast, you slowed down. That's not nothing.
You are doing better than you think.
Breathe in. You are a gift. Not just to others. To yourself.
closing: As this practice ends, let the feeling of gratitude stay warm in your chest.
You don't have to hold onto it tightly. It will echo.
Tomorrow, try to notice one small good thing. Just one.
That's how this practice grows. One moment at a time.
Open your eyes gently. The world looks a little different now.
